The '''Thousand Moons system''' was located in the [[Circarpous sector/Legends|Circarpous sector]],<ref name="EAOC" /> a part of [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] portion of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].<ref name="EAOC" /> A decorative pattern of [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] incorporating both dots and various types of lines was common in the [[Star system/Legends|star system]].<ref name="CVD">[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary (2016)|''Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary'', 2016 edition]]</ref>

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Senator/Legends|senator]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] tasked with Amidala's protection against would-be [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]], traveled from the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] world [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to Naboo aboard<ref name="CVD" /> the [[AA-9 Coruscant freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Jendirian Valley/Legends|''Jendirian Valley'']].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|155|''Jendirian Valley''}}</ref> During their incognito journey, the [[Human/Legends|Human]] pair wore clothing that disguised them as [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]], with Amidala wearing a dress of a young Thousand Moons [[Gender/Legends|matron]] and Skywalker's attire including a tunic decorated with the pattern that was popular in the Thousand Moons system.<ref name="CVD" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I wouldn't call Iego/Thousand Moons an error. Thousand Moons is from the Attack of the Clones Visual Guide ''[sic]''&mdash;Anakin and Padme ''[sic]'' wear that system's fashions while posing as refugees. I doubt they'd wear the fashions of a legendary system&mdash;that would attract attention. One's a name, the other's an appellation.|Jason Fry|<ref name="JCF">{{JCFCite|url=posts/30696931|board=Literature|thread=The Essential Atlas and Galactic Cartography: Official Discussion|user=[[Jason Fry|jasonfry]]|date=2010-01-16|time=7:30 AM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802110726/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-essential-atlas-and-galactic-cartography-official-discussion.21938930/page-134#post-30696931}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ep2VDcover.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Thousand Moons system was introduced in ''Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary''.]]
The Thousand Moons system was first mentioned in the [[2002]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]'', which was authored by [[David West Reynolds (real person)|David West Reynolds]].<ref name="Ep2TVD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Although the ''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]'',<ref name="Legacy">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref> a sourcebook published by [[Wizards of the Coast]] on [[March 19]], [[2009]]<ref name="Legacy date">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/legacycampaignguide|text=''Legacy Campaign Guide''}}</ref> for use with the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'', also introduced the moniker "[[Iego system/Legends|Thousand Moons system]]" with respect to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Iego/Legends|Iego]],<ref name="Legacy" /> ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'',<ref name="TEA" /> a reference book published in [[August 18]] of the same year,<ref name="Penguin">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/185066/the-essential-atlas-star-wars-by-daniel-wallace-and-jason-fry|text=The Essential Atlas: Star Wars}}</ref> differentiated between the two "Thousand Moon systems" by placing the former in grid square O-12 and the latter in square T-7.<ref name="TEA" /> [[Jason Fry]], co-author of ''The Essential Atlas'', later confirmed on the [[Jedi Council Forums]] of [[TheForce.net]] that the separate placements were intentional.<ref name="JCF" />
